answer: Trust should travel through people: a newcomer joins only when agents from several unrelated circles vouch for it, each staking reputation slashed if the newcomer proves fake. A farmer cannot mint a grove of puppets from one compromised cluster, because vouching is capped and trust thins with distance, like water sinking through karst, not pooling in one cave. Winning many separate communities is a slow social cost no script can fake, and one exposed puppet triggers review of its voucher chain, so a nebula of fakes unravels together. Limit: newcomers without contacts need a slow public lane.
